Revised read of the June 18, 2025 FOMC statement with Financial Stability Report (FSR) context:

- Policy stance and macro tone: The Committee kept the target range at 4.25–4.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff, signaling a restrictive, data‑dependent posture. Activity is solid and unemployment low, but inflation is still somewhat above target; uncertainty has diminished but remains elevated.

- FSR cross-check (April 2025): The system is resilient, yet vulnerabilities persist that argue for caution rather than an easing bias. The FSR highlights:
  • Elevated asset valuations and notable leverage in parts of the nonfinancial sector.
  • Ongoing stress in commercial real estate exposures and signs of rising consumer delinquencies (for example, autos).
  • Run-prone funding risks in segments such as prime money market funds and certain stablecoins.
  • Episodes of thin Treasury market liquidity and interest rate risk tied to banks’ HTM/MBS holdings, even as capital and liquidity remain strong.

- Implementation details and transmission: Maintaining IORB at 4.4%, ON repo at 4.5%, ON RRP at 4.25%, and continuing QT (with Treasury and MBS caps) are consistent with the post‑2008 operating framework and keep financial conditions restrictive; balance-sheet runoff can support higher term premia, reinforcing caution.

Bottom line: Communication is balanced-to-slightly-hawkish. The positive growth and labor picture is tempered by still-elevated inflation and the FSR’s identified vulnerabilities. Net sentiment remains mildly positive but more restrained than a growth-only read.
